request.legal_values: bank is less than BANK_COUNT; host-originated row[9:2] and column[5:2] are zero.

semantics.ACT: Open bank at row; column and wdata are zero.
semantics.PRE: Close bank; row, column, and wdata are zero.
semantics.READ: Access matching open bank row and column; wdata is zero.
semantics.WRITE: Access matching open bank row and column with wdata.
semantics.REF: All-bank refresh; bank, row, column, and wdata are zero.

clock_reset.handshake_gating: Suppress all valid, ready, admission, dispatch, commit, response-delivery, and refresh events while rst_n is low.

timing_rules.edge_convention: A trigger committed at edge E permits a blocked command at E+T when all other conditions hold. Reset creates no timing history. tFAW counts earlier ACT commits whose age at the candidate edge is strictly less than its window.

system.rules.R1.statement: Implement global FIFO service in acceptance order, including same-address writes and reads. Admit on every rising-edge txn_valid && txn_ready, independently of command readiness.

system.rules.R2.statement: Provide four waiting entries plus one separately stored active request. Dispatch only previously stored requests, capture the complete pre-edge head before releasing its slot, and permit full-queue simultaneous dispatch/admission including capacity one. No empty-queue bypass or same-edge active replacement at retirement.

system.rules.R3.statement: Use explicit NOP/ACT/PRE/READ/WRITE/REF command semantics, with NOP never committed and at most one command commit per edge. Sequence closed banks with ACT-access, row hits with access, and row conflicts with PRE-ACT-access. PRE/ACT never retire the active request. Keep blocked candidates stable through stalls and newly pending refresh.

system.rules.R4.statement: Keep separate owners for host mapping, waiting storage, scheduling, command sequencing, row state, timing, functional memory/responses, and refresh control. The top must contain structural connections only.

system.rules.R5.statement: Update bank state and timing history only from committed commands. Enforce tRCD, tRAS, tRP, tRRD, tFAW and tRFC using the selected project profile. A trigger at E permits the blocked command at E+T; tFAW counts earlier ACT commits with age strictly less than its window. Reset creates no synthetic timing history.

system.rules.R6.statement: Preserve functional banked 32-bit memory and compact host address mapping. WRITE commit updates storage; READ commit at E captures pre-edge data and registers valid/data for host sampling at E+1, with no extra adapter response register. Responses survive active release, cleanup and refresh; writes produce no response.

system.rules.R7.statement: Open-page retains rows. Support close-page as a configurable alternative, retaining a separate cleanup bank reservation after retirement until a legal PRE commits; block new dispatch during cleanup.

system.rules.R8.statement: Generate periodic refresh deadlines from the last sampled reset edge using tREFI. Coalesce missed deadlines into sticky pending; a due deadline wins over simultaneous REF acknowledgment. Drain active work and cleanup, PRE remaining open banks in ascending order, respect all-bank tRP, commit REF once, and exclude commands strictly before REF-edge+tRFC. Retain queued traffic and resume service afterward.

system.rules.R9.statement: cmd_ready is reset-gated diagnostic readiness for the incoming request's first needed command, using independent row/timing probe queries while the engine is idle and cleanup/refresh permit. It is meaningful without txn_valid and must not admit, dispatch, bypass FIFO, mutate history or reserve storage.

system.rules.R10.statement: Use synchronous active-low reset for state, with immediate valid/ready/event gating. Reset clears queued/active/cleanup work, row state, timing history, memory, responses and refresh state; it wins over every simultaneous event. The host holds payload while stalled and samples every response; no response backpressure is provided.

system.rules.R11.statement: Generate architecture-specific module isolation and system verification intent with exact requirement IDs, independent scenarios/expected results, and declared port/event bindings. Export it alongside RTL for the external UVM/vector stage. Do not execute downstream verification or backend stages in this frontend flow.

system.rules.R12.statement: Explicitly distinguish initial command candidate creation from replacement. Dispatch captures the request without forming a candidate on that edge. When the candidate slot is empty, form the first candidate on a later edge from registered ownership and current bank state. Hold a blocked candidate unchanged. Commit clears its slot; a following candidate is formed only on a later edge using updated bank state, never by same-edge replacement. Reset wins; an outstanding candidate holds or commits before other progress. With no candidate, drain active service, then cleanup, then pending refresh preparation. Refresh service blocks dispatch and new candidate formation. Internal state encoding remains an implementation choice.

system.rules.R13.statement: Define payload behavior independently of valid gating. candidate_command is canonical zero NOP when candidate_valid is low. commit_command mirrors candidate_command even when candidate_ok is low; permission gates commit_valid only, and consumers sample payload only on commit_valid. probe_command remains the combinational first-command query from the incoming request and bank state even when probe_valid is low; idle, cleanup and refresh restrictions gate probe validity/readiness, not its payload. Reset forces all command payloads to zero NOP. Combinational dependencies must include any current-cycle input used to gate payload, not just its valid signal.

system.rules.BASE_HOST.statement: Preserve the existing host ports and widths listed in the baseline contract. Accept a request only on a rising clk edge with txn_valid && txn_ready. Hold payload while stalled. Consecutive accepted cycles with txn_valid held high are distinct requests. cmd_ready is execution/timing visibility, not the host acceptance handshake. Deassert txn_ready and rsp_valid during reset.

system.rules.BASE_ADDRESS.statement: Preserve the simplified 4-bit txn_addr mapping: row=txn_addr[3:2], column=txn_addr[1:0], zero-extended into the internal 10-bit row and 6-bit column fields. Preserve explicit txn_bank for multi-bank configurations; a single-bank configuration uses bank 0. Internal packed requests retain bank(2), row(10), column(6), write flag(1), write data(32).

system.rules.BASE_QUEUE.statement: Provide 4 WAITING request slots PLUS one separately stored active-service request: waiting plus active capacity is 5. The active request must not consume a waiting slot. Dispatch captures the complete pre-edge request in active registers and frees its waiting slot without retiring the transaction. A full queue may admit on the same edge as dispatch; retirement alone does not free waiting storage. Accepted request fields survive stalls and each accepted request is serviced exactly once within a reset-free epoch. Keep admission, dispatch, retirement and read response delivery distinct. Captured response storage consumes neither waiting nor active capacity.

system.rules.BASE_DATA.statement: Provide functional 32-bit memory storage with 16 addresses per bank, bank isolation and reset-to-zero contents. Accepted writes update only their addressed location at service completion or a committed WRITE. Each accepted read produces exactly one one-cycle rsp_valid pulse with the stored rsp_rdata after read service/READ commit, using the existing one-cycle response stage. Writes produce no host response. Selection and stalled candidates cannot mutate memory; mere command output without storage and read responses is insufficient.

system.rules.BASE_TIMING.statement: Retain existing tRCD, tRAS and tRP timing protection from the selected JEDEC profile. ACT-to-READ/WRITE must wait tRCD, ACT-to-PRE must respect tRAS, and PRE-to-next-ACT must respect tRP if explicit commands are used. Aggregate service may retain the existing protected timing envelope instead. Configured tRRD and tFAW gates must use accepted activation events, not host admissions or stalled proposals. Never treat existing basic timing as an unrequested future feature.

system.rules.BASE_SEQUENCE.statement: Dispatch captures the complete selected request in separate active-service registers before freeing its waiting queue slot. Hold that active request and payload across setup PRE/ACT and timing stalls until its final READ/WRITE commits. Setup commands never retire the active request. Aggregate service also keeps active-service ownership through completion. Waiting-queue dequeue at dispatch is distinct from active-request retirement. Row state changes only on the responsible committed operation; uncommitted proposals cannot change state.

system.rules.BASE_MODULARITY.statement: Keep request storage, request selection, command sequencing, timing enforcement and functional memory in independently verifiable modules with explicit interfaces. No single controller core may own all these functions. Each mandatory role has distinct module owners with functional inter-module connections. Module names and further decomposition remain design choices.

system.rules.BASE_LEGALITY.statement: Compute command permission from registered timing/bank history and an independent candidate. An accepted ACT pulse is derived from candidate && permission; permission must not combinationally depend on that same accepted pulse. Scheduler selection/validity must be available independently of timing_ok; timing_ok may gate commit but must not create a selection-validity feedback loop. Declare accurate per-output combinational input dependencies.

system.rules.BASE_RESET.statement: Use top-level clk and active-low rst_n. Reset clears pending requests, active service, row validity, memory and responses. Preserve reusable blocks with either synchronous or asynchronous active-low resets driven by the same rst_n; differing assertion styles do not require rebuilding otherwise reusable blocks. Do not change polarity without an explicit adapter.

system.rules.BASE_POLICY.statement: Honor the requested scheduler policy fifo. Preserve page policy open_page. Open-page retains a serviced row; close-page closes it before subsequent bank use. Preserve request ownership through any setup sequence. Internal module decomposition and command latency may change while these observable contracts hold.

system.rules.BASE_REFRESH.statement: Retain periodic refresh requests using profile tREFI, refresh priority and request/acknowledgment handling without dropping queued traffic. Refresh must make progress and normal requests must resume. Existing refresh is simplified; full REF/tRFC servicing remains later feature work. If explicit REF is proposed, describe drain/row-state interaction and acknowledge once at commit.

system.rules.BASE_TRRD.statement: tRRD is enabled; honor that setting and resolve enabled timing values from DDR4-3200.

system.rules.BASE_TFAW.statement: tFAW is enabled; honor that setting and resolve enabled timing values from DDR4-3200.

system.rules.SYS_SIMULTANEOUS.statement: Reset wins over every event. With reset inactive, admission may coincide with command commit. Full waiting storage may admit on a dispatch edge using the pre-edge head for dispatch and the incoming request for the tail. Dispatch and retirement do not coincide because active ownership remains occupied through retirement. A refresh due coincident with REF commit leaves pending asserted.

system.rules.SYS_STORAGE.statement: Waiting storage holds admitted undispatched requests, active storage holds one dispatched unretired request, and response storage holds one captured read response. These capacities are independent. Dispatch release is not retirement.

execution.rules.EXEC_COMMIT.statement: candidate_command is the canonical proposal. commit_command mirrors it even when candidate_ok is low. commit_valid requires reset inactive, valid candidate, permission, and non-NOP nonreserved opcode. At most one command commits per edge and all consumers sample the same payload only on commit_valid.

execution.rules.EXEC_BANK_STATE.statement: Only committed ACT opens and records its bank row, committed PRE closes its bank, and committed REF clears all rows after preparation. READ and WRITE retain open rows. Probes, proposals, admissions, dispatches, and stalls do not alter row state.

execution.rules.EXEC_RESPONSE.statement: READ commit at E captures pre-edge memory data and registers rsp_valid and rsp_rdata for host sampling at E+1. Delivery and a new READ may share an edge: the host samples the old response before replacement. Writes produce no response.

execution.rules.EXEC_REFRESH.statement: The first deadline is the last reset-sampled edge plus tREFI; later deadlines advance by tREFI independently of REF. Pending is sticky. Pending blocks dispatch and candidate creation after outstanding candidate or active work resolves, drains cleanup, closes remaining open banks in ascending order, waits all-bank tRP, commits REF once, and excludes commands strictly before REF-edge+tRFC.

execution.rules.EXEC_CLEANUP.statement: Open-page creates no cleanup reservation after retirement. Close-page reserves the serviced bank until legal PRE commit, blocks dispatch, and does not duplicate retirement or response. Refresh preparation waits for cleanup.

execution.rules.EXEC_PAYLOAD.statement: candidate_command is zero NOP when candidate_valid is low. A blocked valid candidate remains unchanged. probe_command is the combinational first-command query from incoming mapped request and registered bank state even when probe validity is low. Reset forces all command payloads to zero NOP.

execution.rules.EXEC_PERMISSION.statement: Permission uses registered timing history, registered bank state, independent candidate, and selected bindings. ACT requires closed bank; READ/WRITE require matching open row; PRE requires open bank; REF requires all banks closed and all-bank tRP. Permission does not depend on same-edge commit or updates.

execution.rules.EXEC_READY.statement: txn_ready reflects only waiting admission capacity including same-edge dispatch release. cmd_ready is reset-gated diagnostic first-command readiness using independent row and timing probes while idle and permitted by cleanup and refresh state. Neither diagnostic alters state.

system.verification.V_IDENTITY.expected: The design name is ddr4_controller_top and design kind is memory_controller.

system.verification.V_CONFIGURATION.scenario: Inspect parameters, profile selection, timing bindings, and recorded decisions.
system.verification.V_CONFIGURATION.expected: Open-page default, refresh, FIFO, tFAW, tRRD, DDR4-3200, current_controller baseline, and four-bank topology are recorded.

system.verification.V_HOST.scenario: Hold valid and payload through stalls and across consecutive ready cycles.
system.verification.V_HOST.expected: Only valid-and-ready rising edges admit requests; consecutive qualifying edges are distinct; cmd_ready never substitutes for txn_ready.

system.verification.V_ADDRESS.expected: row, column, bank, widths, and packed request fields follow the declared compact mapping.

system.verification.V_FIFO.scenario: Accept mixed read/write traffic including same-address write/read pairs, row hits, misses, and timing stalls.
system.verification.V_FIFO.expected: Dispatch and retirement follow acceptance order exactly; command readiness does not control admission; younger requests never bypass older requests.

system.verification.V_CAPACITY.scenario: Fill waiting storage, stall active service, dispatch at full occupancy, admit concurrently with dispatch, and retire with queued work.
system.verification.V_CAPACITY.expected: Four waiting entries and one active request coexist; full waiting storage admits on dispatch; retirement alone does not free waiting storage; no empty-queue bypass occurs.

system.verification.V_EXACTLY_ONCE.scenario: Apply long timing stalls, refresh delays, repeated queue reuse, and mixed traffic in a reset-free epoch.
system.verification.V_EXACTLY_ONCE.expected: Each admitted request is dispatched and serviced once with no loss, duplication, or premature retirement.

system.verification.V_SEQUENCE.scenario: Service closed-bank, row-hit, and row-conflict requests while candidates stall.
system.verification.V_SEQUENCE.expected: Closed banks use ACT then access, hits use access, conflicts use PRE then ACT then access, and setup commands do not retire active work.

bindings.note: Check closed, hit, and conflict sequences.

system.verification.V_CANDIDATE.scenario: Dispatch, create, stall, commit, and attempt same-edge replacement; repeat when refresh becomes pending.
system.verification.V_CANDIDATE.expected: Dispatch creates no candidate; blocked candidates hold; commit clears the slot; later creation uses updated state; refresh blocks new creation.

bindings.note: Check delayed creation and later replacement.

system.verification.V_TIMING.scenario: Test trigger and blocked commands at E+T-1 and E+T, including global ACT spacing and four prior ACTs.
system.verification.V_TIMING.expected: Only committed commands update history; permission is independent of its own acceptance; no command commits early; exact boundaries are eligible when other conditions hold.

system.verification.V_MEMORY.scenario: Write and read every compact address in every bank, overlap response delivery with later reads, and reset during response visibility.
system.verification.V_MEMORY.expected: WRITE updates only its addressed word; READ captures pre-edge data and yields one E+1 response; banks isolate; reset zeros memory and cancels validity.

system.verification.V_PAGE.scenario: Run equivalent traffic under both page-policy values and assert refresh during close-page cleanup.
system.verification.V_PAGE.expected: Open-page retains rows; close-page reserves cleanup until legal PRE, blocks dispatch during cleanup, and does not duplicate retirement or response.

system.verification.V_REFRESH.scenario: Cause deadlines while idle, active, candidate-blocked, cleanup-active, and during REF acknowledgment.
system.verification.V_REFRESH.expected: Deadlines coalesce; active and cleanup drain; banks close ascending; REF occurs after all-bank tRP; due with REF leaves pending; traffic resumes after tRFC.

bindings.note: Predict drain, REF, exclusion, and resume.

system.verification.V_DIAGNOSTIC.scenario: Vary incoming request, row state, timing, txn_valid, engine busy state, cleanup, refresh, reset, and queue occupancy.
system.verification.V_DIAGNOSTIC.expected: cmd_ready is reset-gated first-command diagnostic readiness, meaningful without txn_valid, and has no admission, dispatch, storage, history, or commit side effect.

bindings.note: Check diagnostic side effects are absent.

system.verification.V_RESET.scenario: Assert reset during every defined event and visible response condition.
system.verification.V_RESET.expected: Events and valid/ready outputs are gated while reset is low; reset clears specified state and defeats simultaneous nonreset actions.

system.verification.V_ISOLATION.scenario: Review future architecture export against required functional responsibilities.
system.verification.V_ISOLATION.expected: Distinct independently verifiable functional responsibilities and a structural-only top are declared without selecting an architecture here.

system.verification.V_PAYLOAD.scenario: Vary candidate valid, permission, probe valid, idle restrictions, refresh restrictions, and reset independently.
system.verification.V_PAYLOAD.expected: Invalid candidate and reset command payloads are zero NOP; commit payload mirrors candidate; probe payload remains independently defined.

bindings.note: Check NOP masking and independent probe payload.

system.verification.V_EXPORT.scenario: Inspect this package before downstream UVM/vector use.
system.verification.V_EXPORT.expected: Requirement IDs, scenarios, expected outcomes, and declared interfaces/events are present; no downstream execution or backend completion is claimed.

execution.verification.X_COMMIT.scenario: Present legal commands, NOP, reserved opcodes, blocked candidates, and simultaneous admissions.
execution.verification.X_COMMIT.expected: Only permitted legal candidates commit once per edge and noncommits have no commit effects.

execution.verification.X_BANK.scenario: Commit ACT, PRE, READ, WRITE, and REF across banks and compare with stalled proposals.
execution.verification.X_BANK.expected: Only responsible committed operations alter row state.

bindings.note: Compare rows only against committed operations.

execution.verification.X_RESPONSE.scenario: Commit consecutive reads, overlap delivery with a new READ, issue writes, and reset during response visibility.
execution.verification.X_RESPONSE.expected: Each READ yields exactly one E+1 sampled response with pre-edge data; writes yield none.

execution.verification.X_REFRESH.scenario: Run deadlines through active, stalled candidate, cleanup, multiple open banks, tRFC exclusion, and due/REF coincidence.
execution.verification.X_REFRESH.expected: Pending coalesces without traffic loss; close order is ascending; no command commits early after REF; service resumes afterward.

execution.verification.X_CLEANUP.scenario: Retire accesses under both page-policy values and assert refresh during close-page cleanup.
execution.verification.X_CLEANUP.expected: Open-page retains rows; close-page blocks dispatch until one legal PRE and does not duplicate effects.

execution.verification.X_PAYLOAD.scenario: Observe payloads while validity, permission, probe gating, refresh, cleanup, and reset vary.
execution.verification.X_PAYLOAD.expected: Invalid and reset payloads are zero NOP, blocked candidate payload holds, and probe payload is independently defined.

execution.verification.X_PERMISSION.scenario: Test every trigger/block pair one cycle before and at its exact timing bound.
execution.verification.X_PERMISSION.expected: Permission derives only from pre-edge registered state and becomes eligible only at declared boundaries.

execution.verification.X_READY.scenario: Vary occupancy, dispatch opportunity, incoming command type, row/timing state, txn_valid, cleanup, refresh, and reset.
execution.verification.X_READY.expected: txn_ready tracks admission capacity only and cmd_ready is side-effect-free diagnostic readiness.

admission.condition: At a rising clk edge, rst_n is high and pre-edge txn_valid and txn_ready are high.
admission.effect: Capture one complete mapped request into waiting storage.

dispatch.condition: At a rising clk edge, rst_n is high, active ownership is absent, cleanup and refresh service are absent, no candidate is outstanding, and a pre-edge FIFO head is selected.
dispatch.effect: Capture the complete pre-edge FIFO head into active ownership and release exactly that waiting entry.

candidate_create.condition: At a rising clk edge, rst_n is high, active ownership exists, candidate storage is empty, refresh preparation or service is not selected, and no command commits on that edge.
candidate_create.effect: Create a candidate from registered active ownership and registered bank state.

command_commit.condition: At a rising clk edge, rst_n is high, candidate_valid and candidate_ok are high, and candidate_command is non-NOP and nonreserved.
command_commit.effect: Commit one command and update only state assigned to that committed opcode.

retirement.condition: shared.events.command_commit commits READ or WRITE for the active request.
retirement.effect: Retire one active request; READ captures response state before active release.

response_delivery.condition: At a rising clk edge, rst_n is high and pre-edge rsp_valid is high.

refresh_due.condition: At a rising clk edge, rst_n is high and the periodic deadline reaches that edge.
refresh_due.effect: Set sticky refresh pending; simultaneous REF acknowledgment cannot clear newly due pending.

refresh_start.effect: Acknowledge one pending refresh and begin tRFC command exclusion.

refresh_end.condition: At a rising clk edge, rst_n is high and the edge is at least tRFC cycles after committed REF.

clock_reset.handshake_gating: Suppress all valid, ready, admission, dispatch, commit, response-delivery, and refresh events while rst_n is low.

candidate_create.reason: No observable creation pulse exists; independently infer creation from candidate outputs and declared later-edge rules.

refresh_due.reason: Deadline state is internal; independently predict tREFI deadlines from reset and observe refresh state.

refresh_end.reason: No end pulse is exported; independently measure tRFC from committed REF and observe refresh_busy.

system.verification.V_DIAGNOSTIC.note: Check diagnostic side effects are absent.

system.verification.V_REFRESH.note: Predict drain, REF, exclusion, and resume.

system.verification.V_SEQUENCE.note: Check closed, hit, and conflict sequences.

system.verification.V_CANDIDATE.note: Check delayed creation and later replacement.

system.verification.V_PAYLOAD.note: Check NOP masking and independent probe payload.

execution.verification.X_BANK.note: Compare rows only against committed operations.

limitations: candidate_create: No observable creation pulse exists; independently infer creation from candidate outputs and declared later-edge rules.
refresh_due: Deadline state is internal; independently predict tREFI deadlines from reset and observe refresh state.
refresh_end: No end pulse is exported; independently measure tRFC from committed REF and observe refresh_busy.

D_FIFO.reason: Accepted requests are serviced in FIFO acceptance order.

D_CAPACITY.reason: Waiting and active capacities are distinct.

D_COMMANDS.reason: Explicit command semantics and commit gating are required.

D_PAGE_POLICY.reason: Open-page is requested while close-page is a configurable alternative.

D_REFRESH.reason: Refresh deadlines coalesce and service drains work before REF.

D_RESET.reason: State reset is synchronous and all externally visible events are immediately gated.

D_RESPONSE.reason: READ captures pre-edge data and provides the requested one-cycle response stage.

A_CLOCK.statement: clk continues to provide rising edges while rst_n is low so synchronous reset state clearing can occur.

A_HOST_STALL.statement: The host holds txn_valid and all transaction payload fields stable while txn_valid is high and txn_ready is low.

A_RESPONSE.statement: The host samples every rsp_valid pulse because no response-backpressure interface is provided.

A_PROGRESS.statement: Service progress requires reset to remain inactive and timing and refresh intervals to elapse; no bounded transaction latency is asserted.

A_PROFILE.statement: The selected timing library supplies the declared DDR4-3200 timing paths.

strategy.module_checks: Future downstream checks shall independently isolate admission and storage, FIFO selection, command candidate and commit behavior, timing permission, row state, functional memory and responses, refresh, and host diagnostics through declared interfaces.
strategy.system_scenario: Apply directed and randomized host traffic with independent FIFO, command-trace, timing, memory, response, refresh, reset, and diagnostic scoreboards.
strategy.system_evidence: Planned evidence includes per-rule assertions, directed vectors, randomized traces, commit-edge monitors, timing-boundary checks, reset checks, and coverage of simultaneous events.

blocking_reasons.detail: The existing discovery entry point does not read this handoff schema.
The current orchestrator publisher reads frontend-root rtl_output/manifest.json; it does not select an isolated architecture build or this handoff automatically.
System discovery expects legacy component configuration/master specs, a frontend testbench, and clock/reset inferred from sequential logic in the top.
The existing UVM adapter expects legacy top-level private signals; this export binds declared module ports.
Existing system reference semantics permit pre-dispatch reordering and build their own SYS-REQ catalog. New requirement IDs and semantics need explicit consumer support.

rules: Preserve source IDs; any consumer-ID translation must be explicit.
Only an rtl-phase handoff with an RTL revision can identify a DUT for runtime verification.
Missing records remain unverified; successful generation/compilation is not behavioral evidence.
Passed requires executed checks and evidence; not_applicable requires a justified configuration-specific reason.
Identity mismatch, duplicate/unknown IDs, or missing evidence must not be accepted as a pass.
